questions.q: What is a scoped application, as described in this lesson?
options: A contained namespace that keeps a team's custom tables, scripts, and logic separate from the base platform and other teams' customizations
A third-party application hosted entirely outside ServiceNow
A read-only reporting dashboard with no custom logic
A ServiceNow certification exam format
questions.explain: Scoped applications contain custom development so it doesn't collide with base-system or other teams' customizations.

questions.q: Which three earlier courses in this path does ServiceNow Developer work draw on most directly?
options: Course 1 (ITSM/ITIL 4 Foundations), course 9 (CMDB/CSDM), and course 12 (Performance Troubleshooting)
Course 5 (JavaScript for ServiceNow), course 6 (Scripting & Application Development), and course 7 (IntegrationHub & REST APIs)
Course 3 (System Administration) and course 10 (Security & Access Controls) only
Course 13 (Technical Architecture) and course 14 (Career & Capstone)
questions.explain: The lesson ties scoped application development, scripting, and integrations directly back to courses 5, 6, and 7.

questions.q: What distinguishes a Client Script from a Business Rule?
options: A Client Script runs in the user's browser to control form behavior in real time; a Business Rule runs server-side on record events
There is no functional difference between them
Business Rules only run when a user clicks a button
Client Scripts can only be used inside Service Portal widgets
questions.explain: Client Scripts execute client-side (browser) for real-time form behavior; Business Rules execute server-side on insert/update/delete/query events.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what's the key difference between a ServiceNow Developer and a generic software developer?
options: A ServiceNow Developer typically builds within the platform's existing data layer, UI framework, and workflow engine, rather than standing up custom infrastructure from scratch
ServiceNow Developers never write any code at all
ServiceNow Developers and generic software developers do functionally identical work with no meaningful distinction
ServiceNow Developers exclusively work on hardware provisioning
questions.explain: Most ServiceNow development happens inside the platform's own framework rather than requiring custom infrastructure decisions.

questions.q: Why does the lesson suggest naming specific building blocks (Business Rules, Script Includes, widgets, REST integrations) in an interview?
options: It demonstrates real, specific platform fluency, versus a generic "I'm a developer" answer that signals a possible gap in platform-native experience
Interviewers only care about job titles, not technical specifics
Naming specific tools guarantees a job offer regardless of experience
It's required by ServiceNow's certification program
questions.explain: Specific, accurate platform vocabulary signals real fluency with how ServiceNow development actually works, which is what interviewers are listening for.
